articles.title: Bestselling Japanese Novelist Maha Harada Says ‘If This Is a Dream, I Hope I Never Wake Up’ About Her San Sebastian – and Busan – Bound Directing Debut ‘In My Father’s Room’
articles.summary: Maha Harada spent two decades building scenes on the page before she ever stood behind a camera. Now 64, the best-selling Japanese author is making her feature directorial debut with “In My Father’s Room,” a film adapted from her own short story “An Unnecessary Man,” and it arrives in competition…
body: Ahead of both stops, Bitters End has already sold the film to France, Korea, Taiwan and Hong Kong, with more territories under discussion.

That story follows Satomi, an art museum worker who learns almost nothing about her father, Yuichi, until after he has died alone. Harada says the character grew directly out of her own family. Her father sold art books, loved film and gambling, and “never stopped causing trouble,” she says, but he also introduced her to Picasso at age 10 and took her to see “Gone with the Wind” and “The Castle of Sand” at 12. It was only once he was gone, she says, that she understood how much he had taught her.

articles.title: ‘Still feel a jolt of joy’: why Dirty Dancing is my feelgood movie
articles.summary: The latest in our ongoing series of writers highlighting their most rewatched comfort films remembers a 1987 teenage girl classic. There is probably a Swedish word for the emotional state engendered in me by Dirty Dancing.
body: The movie must have seemed quite raunchy to me then. Light on actual sex, but heavy on petting during extended scenes of hot, fully-clothed couples grinding to a soundtrack of objectively incredible music. Catnip, then, for curious tweenage girls.

For several years, Dirty Dancing was the wallpaper to every sleepover I went to. Its catchphrases were social currency at my girls’ school. Shouting “I carried a watermelon,” or “nobody puts Baby in the corner!” across a crowded classroom signaled a nuanced understanding of the Year 7 zeitgeist. And, of course, we all tried to do the lift. So many memories of uniformed girls landing on top of other uniformed girls at break time; so many scraped knees and elbows.

articles.title: Sean Hogan’s ‘The Dark Gets In’ Boarded for Worldwide Sales by Blue Finch Films Ahead of Beyond Fest Bow (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Blue Finch Films has boarded worldwide sales rights to “The Dark Gets In,” a supernatural thriller directed by Sean Hogan that will premiere at Beyond Fest later this month.
body: In a statement, Hogan said: “‘The Dark Gets In’ is based upon an idea I had several years ago, but it wasn’t until I hit upon the notion of telling it in a true crime mockumentary format that it finally found its proper expression. We set out to make a film that initially felt very real and disturbing, but would eventually reveal itself to be something far more horrifying than the sort of story you typically see in such documentaries. The end result is, I hope, a mixture of tragedy and tension and slow-burning dread, and I’m excited to see how audiences respond to its many shocks and surprises.”

Ersoy, who also produced “To Fire You Come At Last” with Hogan, added: “After the success of ‘To Fire You Come At Last,’ another opportunity to work with Sean was only natural – and with ‘The Dark Gets In,’ he has crafted a singularly unique film that delivers on the promise of its eerie atmosphere and will hopefully scare audiences around the world with its unique blend of the supernatural and true crime.”

articles.title: Tobias Forge’s ‘V/H/S Mixtape’ Segment, Swedish Horror ‘Trespassers,’ ‘The End’ by ‘Midsommar’ Production Designer on Mylla Films Slate (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Swedish boutique genre specialist Mylla Films, brainchild of “Midsommar” producer Patrik Andersson and Nordic indie distribution heavyweight Jakob Abrahamsson (CEO of NonStop Entertainment), has turned into a magnet for Nordic genre talent since its splashy launch in Cannes in 2022.
body: The five minutes and a half clip, starring Gustav Hammarsten (“Brüno,” “The Girl With the Dragon Tattoo”) and Nour el-Refai (“Jordskott,” “The Bonus Family”), is “an old school story-driven death metal music video,” said the versatile Andersson, himself a seasoned musician.

“We were contacted in June and managed to turn around Tobias’ segment in three months. It’s been extremely fun and frankly astonishing!” said Abrahamsson, who will release “V/H/S/ Mixtape” in the Nordics via NonStop Entertainment.

Another of Mylla Films’ recent recruits is Henrik Svensson, production designer of Ari Aster’s “Midsommar” and Kristoffer Borgli’s “Sick of Myself,” now making his directorial debut with the low budget “The End.”

“The End,” which is fully-financed by private equity coin and stars prolific Swedish author Mattias Ribbing, is described by Andersson as “an avant-garde experimental audiovisual film featuring literally killing soundtracks,” with stunts designed by “Kung Fury’s” Eos Karlsson. “We’ve tried to do a Jodorowsky film in Sweden, which has been lots of fun. We can’t wait to showcase it,” said Andersson, who’s eying a genre festival launchpad in the spring 2027.

articles.title: Legend of the White Dragon review – Power Rangers alumni back for more in low-budget superhero retread
articles.summary: Simple but emphatic martial arts and a couple of classy cameos are all that give this blandly modern action film a fighting chance. Despite featuring a clutch of Power Rangers graduates, including Jason David Frank, who died in 2022, this crowdfunded effort is beholden to a more recent action…
body: Considering the presumably teeny budget, Legend of the White Dragon manages a fair approximation of the lacquered hi-tech blockbuster look, and calls in a couple of classy cameos: Michael Madsen, giving the lore a gravitas boost, and Mark Dacascos, who can do kung fu monk blindfolded. The many martial arts sequences are simple but emphatic, in the Power Rangers style. But Schoenke, directing with his father, Sean, unbalances his own film by the simple fact that his own character – a kind of disintegrating, evil Bruce Wayne – is far more interesting than the protagonist.

The limp Frank is an energy vacuum, typical of a general acting level that makes Marvel look like Merchant Ivory. Not that the sappy interludes between the fisticuffs, focusing on his sins-of-the-father issues and Katua’s ragebait memories of his former family idyll, help. There’s too little here that might lead the superhero genre into offbeat indie pastures, like Chronicle did back in 2012; only Andrew Bachelor’s supercomputer URI, as if JARVIS had been reprogrammed as Chris Rock, hints at the possibilities, sassily repeating “scanning” as the bland superhero crew waits for intel.

articles.title: Presley Gerber, Cindy Crawford's son, dies aged 27
articles.summary: His family asked for privacy during a "very difficult and painful time" following the model's death.
body: Presley Gerber, the son of supermodel Cindy Crawford, has died at the age of 27.
Gerber, a model, died at a rehab facility on Sunday, according to records filed by the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner. The cause of death was not listed.
Allie Jenkins, a representative for Crawford and her husband Rande Gerber, told the BBC's US news partner CBS: "The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time."
Gerber had been a model like his mother and younger sister Kaia, making his runway debut for Italian label Moschino aged just 16.

articles.title: La Bola Negra wins Toronto film festival people’s choice award
articles.summary: The queer period drama wins Oscar-predicting award, being named the most popular audience film at the festival. The Spanish queer drama La Bola Negra has won this year’s people’s choice award at the Toronto film festival.
body: The film, which takes place in 1932, 1937 and 2017, focuses on the lives of interconnected gay men. It premiered at this year’s Cannes film festival with the Guardian’s Peter Bradshaw calling it “handsomely produced, lovingly detailed and confidently constructed” in a four-star review.
After a competitive bidding war after its premiere in May, Netflix picked up the rights and the film will be released later this year.
In a prepared statement, directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi said that connecting with Toronto audiences in this way was “the greatest gift we could receive”.
It marks the first foreign language winner of the award since 2011’s Lebanese drama Where Do We Go Now?

articles.title: John Oliver Takes Jab at “Soon-to-Be Business Daddy” David Ellison on ‘Last Week Tonight’
articles.summary: During a segment on UnitedHealthCare's history of denying claims, Oliver said: "Having access to wealthy parents just cannot be the system to get badly needed healthcare, even if it is apparently the system that lets you be in charge of HBO."
body: John Oliver took a jab at “soon-to-be business daddy” David Ellison on Sunday’s Last Week Tonight.

The HBO show’s host did a deep dive into UnitedHealthCare record of denying customers much-needed health care, starting off by noting that Luigi Mangione is due to be sentenced in December for killing CEO Brian Thompson, an act that many people rejoiced amid their frustration with the company.

Here he took the opportunity to take a jab at Ellison, the CEO of Paramount Skydance, which is in the process of trying to get regulator approval to purchase Warner Bros. Discovery, the current parent company of HBO.

“Yeah, my soon-to-be business daddy has a literal business daddy,” he added, as the image zoomed out to show Ellison with his father Larry, the billionaire owner of tech giant Oracle, and the man who has agreed to personally backstop the $40.4 billion in equity financing connected to the Paramount-WBD deal.

articles.title: 15 Best International Fantasy Movies, Ranked
articles.summary: While there have been plenty of great fantasy films produced in the U.S. and other English-speaking countries, one would be doing a disservice to themselves by not branching out and exploring such films from other territories.
body: The following international fantasy movies offer a sampling of how fascinating the genre is and always has been around the world. The following films come from places around the world, including Spain, Germany, Japan, Sweden, and Mexico, and are ranked below, beginning with the very good and then ending with the titles that can count themselves among the very best fantasy movies ever made.

Magical realism and Latin American literature are so intricately tied together that they're almost inseparable, and Mexico in particular has a delectably rich fantasy tradition. From that history of magical realism came Ernesto Contreras ' I Dream in Another Language, a drama about a linguist ( Fernando Rebeil ) who travels to a Mexican jungle in order to research a dying indigenous language. The only problem? Its last two remaining speakers refuse to talk to each other.
